records.source: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֣יא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֡ה יוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֶת־עַצְמ֣וֹת מַלְכֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֣ה וְאֶת־עַצְמוֹת־שָׂרָיו֩ וְאֶת־עַצְמ֨וֹת הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת׀עַצְמ֣וֹת הַנְּבִיאִ֗ים וְאֵ֛ת עַצְמ֥וֹת יוֹשְׁבֵֽי־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֖ם מִקִּבְרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: In the time the that, declares Yahweh, they will bring out bones of [the] kings of Judah and bones of its princes and bones of the priests and bones of the prophets and bones of [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem from their graves.
pieces: At that time, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the bones of Judah's kings and officials, of the priests and prophets, and of all who lived in Jerusalem will be taken from their graves.

L.1: At that time, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they will bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of its princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem from their graves.

R.1: At that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, people will dig up the bones of the kings and leaders of Judah, the bones of the priests and prophets, and the bones of the people who lived in Jerusalem. They will take them out of their graves.

decisions.choice: at that time: the days of slaughter just announced
decisions.reason: "That time" points back to the days described in 7:32-34, when the dead will fill the valley of Ben-hinnom. God is still speaking to Jeremiah; the message that began at 7:2 ends with verse 3.

decisions.choice: they will bring out: people not named, the invaders
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It means simply that the bones will be brought out; the ones who do it are the enemies who take the city.

decisions.choice: bones taken from graves: the worst disgrace for the dead
decisions.reason: To be buried and left in peace in the family grave was a deep concern in Israel (Genesis 47:29-30; 1 Kings 13:22). Opening tombs, often to rob them, and scattering the bones was the final shame a conquered people could suffer (2 Kings 23:16; Amos 2:1). Every rank of the nation, from its kings down, will suffer it.

decisions.choice: will be taken out (B); people will dig up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the verb with no named subject in the passive; Readable says "people", as the Hebrew means anyone at all.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The word for the king's high officials is rendered the same way through the prophets.

records.source: וּשְׁטָחוּם֩ לַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ וְלַיָּרֵ֜חַ וּלְכֹ֣ל׀צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲהֵב֜וּם וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר עֲבָדוּם֙ וַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ הָלְכ֣וּ אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר דְּרָשׁ֔וּם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם לֹ֤א יֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִקָּבֵ֔רוּ לְדֹ֛מֶן עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה יִֽהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And they will spread them to the sun and to the moon and to all [the] host of the heavens, which they loved them and which they served them and which they walked after them and which they sought them and which they bowed down to them; not they will be gathered and not they will be buried; for dung on [the] face of the ground they will be.
pieces: They will lie spread out under the sun, the moon and the whole host of heaven, which they loved and served, which they followed, consulted and worshiped. No one will gather them or bury them; they will lie like dung on the surface of the ground.

L.2: And they will spread them out before the sun and before the moon and before all the host of the heavens, which they have loved and which they have served and after which they have walked and which they have sought and to which they have bowed down. They will not be gathered and will not be buried; they will be dung on the face of the ground.

R.2: The bones will be spread out on the ground under the sun, the moon and all the stars. The people loved these things in the sky and served them. They followed them, asked them for guidance and bowed down to them. But no one will gather up the bones or bury them. They will lie on the ground like manure.

decisions.choice: the sun, the moon and the host of heaven: the sky gods Judah worshiped, now looking on
decisions.reason: Worship of the sun, moon and stars was forbidden (Deuteronomy 4:19; 17:3), yet King Manasseh built altars to them in the temple courts (2 Kings 21:3-5) and Josiah later removed them (2 Kings 23:4-5, 11). The bones of their worshipers lie open to these powers, which can do nothing to help them.

decisions.choice: loved, served, walked after, sought, bowed down: every kind of devotion
decisions.reason: Five verbs pile up the people's devotion. "Walked after" means followed as a loyal servant follows a master, "sought" means consulted for guidance or an oracle, and "bowed down" is the posture of worship. It is the devotion they owed to the LORD (Deuteronomy 6:5; 10:12).

decisions.choice: dung on the face of the ground: left unburied to rot
decisions.reason: The bodies or bones will lie spread on the fields like manure. Jeremiah uses the picture for the unburied dead several times (9:21; 16:4; 25:33).

decisions.choice: will be spread out; consulted / asked them for guidance; manure (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the passive for the unnamed subject, as in verse 1. Readable says "stars" for the host of heaven, explains "sought" and says "manure" for the dung spread on fields.

records.source: וְנִבְחַ֥ר מָ֨וֶת֙ מֵֽחַיִּ֔ים לְכֹ֗ל הַשְּׁאֵרִית֙ הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֔ים מִן־הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֥ה הָֽרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את בְּכָל־הַמְּקֹמ֤וֹת הַנִּשְׁאָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִדַּחְתִּ֣ים שָׁ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: And will be chosen death rather than life by all the remnant, the remaining [ones], from the family the evil the this, in all the places the remaining where I have driven them there, declares Yahweh of hosts.
pieces: All who are left of this evil family, in every place where I have driven them, will choose death rather than life, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies."

L.3: And death will be chosen rather than life by all the remnant who remain of this evil family, in all the remaining places where I have driven them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts."

R.3: Some people of this evil nation will still be alive, and I will drive them away to other places. But everywhere they are, they will want to die rather than live, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies."

decisions.choice: death will be chosen rather than life: exile will be worse than death
decisions.reason: Moses set life and death before Israel and told them to choose life (Deuteronomy 30:19). Those who survive the fall of the city will find life in exile so bitter that they would rather be dead.

decisions.choice: this evil family: the whole nation, seen as one clan
decisions.reason: The word means a clan or extended family. Here, as in 2:4 and Amos 3:1, it is the whole people descended from one ancestor.

decisions.choice: in all the places where I have driven them: the second "remaining" repeats the word before
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "remaining" twice, the second time after "places", which reads awkwardly ("in all the places the remaining"). It is probably a copyist's repetition of the same word a few words earlier, and the Greek translation (the Septuagint) does not have it. The sense is the same either way: survivors scattered among the nations.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD of hosts: the end of God's message begun at 7:2
decisions.reason: The prose message God gave Jeremiah at the temple gate (7:2) closes here. A new oracle in poetry begins in verse 4.

decisions.choice: in every place / to other places (no second "remaining")
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable do not repeat "remaining", following meaning decision m3; Literal keeps the Hebrew's wording.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: The title is rendered as in Isaiah. Verses 1-3 continue the speech God began at 7:2, so they open no new quotation; the double quotation mark at the end of this verse closes it at every level.

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲיִפְּל֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יָק֑וּמוּ אִם־יָשׁ֖וּב וְלֹ֥א יָשֽׁוּב׃
records.gloss: And you will say to them, Thus says Yahweh: Do they fall and not rise? If one turns away, not does he return?
pieces: Say to them, {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q When people fall, do they not get up again? \q When someone turns away, do they not turn back?

L.4: And you shall say to them, Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Do people fall and not get up? \q If one turns away, does one not turn back?

R.4: Tell them, This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q When people fall down, they get up again. \q When people go the wrong way, they turn around and come back.

decisions.choice: turns away ... turn back: one verb used both ways
decisions.reason: The same verb means both to turn away and to turn back, and in the prophets turning back to God is repentance. Jeremiah plays on it five times in verses 4-6 ("turned away", "turning away", "return", "turns"): Judah turns, but only away (3:12-14, 22).

decisions.choice: do people fall and not get up?: questions that expect "of course they do"
decisions.reason: The questions appeal to ordinary life: anyone who falls gets up, anyone who takes a wrong turn comes back. Verse 5 asks why Judah alone does not.

decisions.choice: you shall say to them: a new message in poetry
decisions.reason: God now gives Jeremiah a new message for the people. It is set as poetry, and God's own words carry no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: statements instead of questions
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into statements of what everyone knows, which is what the questions mean.

records.heading: A people who will not turn back

records.source: מַדּ֨וּעַ שׁוֹבְבָ֜ה הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֛ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מְשֻׁבָ֣ה נִצַּ֑חַת הֶחֱזִ֨יקוּ֙ בַּתַּרְמִ֔ית מֵאֲנ֖וּ לָשֽׁוּב׃
records.gloss: Why has turned away the people the this, Jerusalem, [with] a turning away perpetual? They hold fast to deceit; they refuse to return.
pieces: Why then has this people, Jerusalem, turned away, and kept on turning away? \q They cling to deceit; \q they refuse to come back.

L.5: Why has this people, Jerusalem, turned away with a perpetual turning away? \q They hold fast to deceit; \q they refuse to return.

R.5: So why have the people of Jerusalem turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and never stopped? \q They hold on to lies \q and will not come back.

decisions.choice: turned away with a perpetual turning away: faithlessness that never ends
decisions.reason: The noun from "turn" means turning away from God, faithlessness. Jeremiah uses it for Israel and Judah in 3:6-22 ("faithless Israel"). Here it is "perpetual": they have made a habit of it.

decisions.choice: deceit: lies they tell and lies they believe
decisions.reason: The word means deceit or self-deception. It covers the false words of verse 8 and the false gods they trust (10:14), which they grip and will not let go.

decisions.choice: turned away from me
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one they have turned from, which the Hebrew leaves implied.

records.source: הִקְשַׁ֤בְתִּי וָֽאֶשְׁמָע֙ לוֹא־כֵ֣ן יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אֵ֣ין אִ֗ישׁ נִחָם֙ עַל־רָ֣עָת֔וֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתִי כֻּלֹּ֗ה שָׁ֚ב בִּמְר֣וּצָתָ֔ם כְּס֥וּס שׁוֹטֵ֖ף בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: I have paid attention and I have heard; not right they speak; there is not a man relenting over his wickedness, saying, What have I done? All of it turns in their running, like a horse rushing in battle.
pieces: I have listened closely and heard; they do not speak what is right. \q No one is sorry for their wickedness \q and says, "What have I done?" \q Each of them turns off on their own course, \q like a horse charging into battle.

L.6: I have paid attention and listened; they do not speak what is right. \q No one relents of {{gender:their|his}} wickedness, \q saying, "What have I done?" \q Every one of them turns in their running, \q like a horse rushing into battle.

R.6: I have listened carefully to them, and they do not say what is right. \q No one is sorry for the evil they have done. \q No one says, "What have I done?" \q They all keep running their own way, \q like horses rushing into battle.

decisions.choice: relents: is sorry and changes course
decisions.reason: The verb means to feel sorrow over something and so to change one's mind. Nobody stops to ask "What have I done?", the first step of turning back.

decisions.choice: turns in their running: they do turn, but only to their own headlong course
decisions.reason: "Turns" is the same verb as "return" in verses 4-5. The people do turn, but into their own race, not back to God. The Hebrew as read has a singular noun "course" or "running"; the written letters can be read as plural. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: like a horse rushing into battle: headlong, without stopping to think
decisions.reason: A war horse at the charge cannot be turned (Job 39:21-25). The picture is of people running on in their own way without a pause.

decisions.choice: their / his
decisions.reason: "Man" here means anyone at all, so the Literal pronoun is inclusive by default, with the traditional form as the alternative.

records.source: גַּם־חֲסִידָ֣ה בַשָּׁמַ֗יִם יָֽדְעָה֙ מֽוֹעֲדֶ֔יהָ וְתֹ֤ר וְסִיס֙ וְעָג֔וּרשָׁמְר֖וּ אֶת־עֵ֣ת בֹּאָ֑נָה וְעַמִּ֕י לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ אֵ֖ת מִשְׁפַּ֥ט יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Even a stork in the heavens knows her appointed times, and turtledove and swift and crane keep [the] time of their coming; and my people not know [the] ordinance of Yahweh.
pieces: Even the stork in the sky knows her seasons, \q and the turtledove, the swift and the crane keep the time of their return; \q but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people do not know \q the order {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set.

L.7: Even the stork in the heavens knows her appointed times, \q and the turtledove and the swift and the crane keep the time of their coming; \q but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people do not know \q the ordinance of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.7: Even the stork in the sky knows when it is time to go. \q The dove, the swift and the crane know when to come back. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people do not know \q what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} wants them to do.

decisions.choice: stork, turtledove, swift, crane: birds that migrate through Israel
decisions.reason: Great flocks of birds pass over the land every spring and autumn on their way between Africa and the north, and come back at the same seasons each year. The stork and the turtledove are known; the other two names are less certain. The third may be a swift or a swallow, and the fourth a crane or a kind of thrush (compare Isaiah 38:14, where two of the same words appear).

decisions.choice: swift: the word as read; the letters as written spell "horse"
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text are the same as the word for "horse" in verse 6; the scribes' reading gives the bird's name, which fits the list of birds. The difference is one vowel letter.

decisions.choice: the ordinance of the LORD: the order God has set for his people
decisions.reason: The word means a ruling or the right way of things. Birds follow the order built into their nature without fail; God's people do not know, or will not follow, the order he has given them in his covenant (5:4-5). Isaiah 1:3 makes the same contrast with the ox and the donkey.

decisions.choice: the order the LORD has set (B); what the LORD wants them to do (R)
decisions.reason: "Ordinance" is not an everyday word; Balanced and Readable say what it means here.

records.source: אֵיכָ֤ה תֹֽאמְרוּ֙ חֲכָמִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וְתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה אִתָּ֑נוּ אָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה לַשֶּׁ֣קֶר עָשָׂ֔ה עֵ֖ט שֶׁ֥קֶר סֹפְרִֽים׃
records.gloss: How will you say, Wise [are] we, and [the] instruction of Yahweh [is] with us? Truly, look, into falsehood has made [it] [the] pen of falsehood of scribes.
pieces: How can you say, "We are wise; \q we have the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}"? \q In fact, the lying pen of the scribes \q has turned it into a lie.

L.8: How can you say, "We are wise, \q and the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with us"? \q Truly, look, into falsehood \q the lying pen of the scribes has made it.

R.8: How can you say, "We are wise, \q because we have the teaching of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}"? \q The truth is that the scribes have used their pens to write lies, \q and they have made that teaching false.

decisions.choice: the instruction of the LORD: God's teaching, his written law
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or instruction, and it is the usual word for the law given through Moses (Deuteronomy 31:9-12). The people boast that they possess it, as if having it made them wise, while they do not obey it (verse 9).

decisions.choice: the lying pen of the scribes has made it into falsehood: they have twisted God's instruction in writing
alternatives: the lying pen of the scribes has worked in vain
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated object. Taken as the instruction just named, the scribes have turned it into a lie by the way they wrote it out, explained or added to it. The words can also be read "the lying pen of the scribes has worked for nothing", that is, all their writing is useless.

decisions.choice: scribes: trained writers who copied and taught the law
decisions.reason: Scribes were officials skilled in writing. They kept records for the king (2 Kings 22:3) and copied and explained the written law. Their skill gave weight to the people's claim to be wise.

decisions.choice: because we have ...; the scribes have used their pens to write lies
decisions.reason: Readable states the reason the people claim to be wise and unpacks "the lying pen of the scribes".

records.source: הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ חֲכָמִ֔ים חַ֖תּוּ וַיִּלָּכֵ֑דוּ הִנֵּ֤ה בִדְבַר־יְהוָה֙ מָאָ֔סוּ וְחָכְמַֽת־מֶ֖ה לָהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Are put to shame [the] wise; they are dismayed and are captured; look, [the] word of Yahweh they have rejected, and wisdom of what [is] to them?
pieces: The wise will be put to shame; \q they will be shattered and trapped. \q They have rejected the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q so what kind of wisdom do they have?

L.9: The wise will be put to shame; \q they will be dismayed and caught. \q Look, they have rejected the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q so what wisdom is theirs?

R.9: These wise people will be put to shame. \q They will be terrified and trapped. \q They have rejected the message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q So how can they be wise?

decisions.choice: will be put to shame ... dismayed and caught: what is sure to happen, told as if done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for completed action, used in prophecy for what is certain to come. The judgment is as good as done.

decisions.choice: caught: taken like an animal in a trap
decisions.reason: The verb is used of animals caught in a snare and of people taken prisoner. Their cleverness will not save them from capture.

decisions.choice: they have rejected the word of the LORD; what wisdom do they have?: wisdom begins with God's word
decisions.reason: Keeping God's commands was to be Israel's wisdom in the eyes of the nations (Deuteronomy 4:6). Those who throw away his word have nothing left that deserves the name (compare 9:22-23).

decisions.choice: these wise people; how can they be wise?
decisions.reason: Readable points back to the people of verse 8 who call themselves wise, and turns the question into a plain one.

records.source: לָכֵן֩ אֶתֵּ֨ן אֶת־נְשֵׁיהֶ֜ם לַאֲחֵרִ֗ים שְׂדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ לְי֣וֹרְשִׁ֔ים כִּ֤י מִקָּטֹן֙ וְעַד־גָּד֔וֹל כֻּלֹּ֖ה בֹּצֵ֣עַ בָּ֑צַע מִנָּבִיא֙ וְעַד־כֹּהֵ֔ן כֻּלֹּ֖ה עֹ֥שֶׂה שָּֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: Therefore I will give their wives to others, their fields to dispossessors; for from small and to great, all of it [is] gaining unjust gain; from prophet and to priest, all of it [is] doing falsehood.
pieces: So I will give their wives to others and their fields to conquerors; \q for from the smallest to the greatest, \q all are out for dishonest gain; \q from prophet to priest, \q every one of them deals in lies.

L.10: Therefore I will give their wives to others, their fields to those who take possession; \q for from the least and to the greatest, \q every one of them is gaining unjust gain; \q from prophet and to priest, \q every one of them practices falsehood.

R.10: So I will give their wives to other men, and the people who conquer them will take their fields. \q Everyone wants to get rich by cheating others, \q from the least important person to the most important. \q Even the prophets and the priests \q all tell lies.

decisions.choice: verses 10-12 repeat 6:12-15
decisions.reason: Verses 10-12 say again, with small differences, what 6:12-15 said. Here the first lines are shorter: 6:12 also names their houses and adds "for I will stretch out my hand"; here there are no houses, and the fields go to "those who take possession". 6:13 says "from their least to their greatest"; here it is "from least to greatest". The rest of the words are the same, and they are rendered the same way.

decisions.choice: the repeated lines are part of the Hebrew text here
decisions.reason: The Greek translation (the Septuagint) does not have the second half of verse 10 or verses 11-12, perhaps because they had already appeared in chapter 6. The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: those who take possession: the conquerors who seize the land
decisions.reason: The word means those who take over property as heirs or by conquest. The enemy will take what Judah thought was its own; it is the curse for breaking the covenant (Deuteronomy 28:30).

decisions.choice: gaining unjust gain: seeking profit by any means
decisions.reason: As in 6:13. The phrase means to cut off a share for oneself, profit got by violence or fraud (22:17; Ezekiel 22:27).

decisions.choice: the wording of 6:13
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew is the same as 6:13, each level uses the same wording as there. Readable says "other men" because the wives are taken by the conquerors.

records.source: וַיְרַפּ֞וּ אֶת־שֶׁ֤בֶר בַּת־עַמִּי֙ עַל־נְקַלָּ֔ה לֵאמֹ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם׀שָׁל֑וֹם וְאֵ֖ין שָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And they have healed [the] fracture of [the] daughter of my people lightly, saying, Peace, peace, and there is not peace.
pieces: They have treated the fracture of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear people as though it were slight, \q saying, "Peace, peace," \q when there is no peace.

L.11: And they have healed the fracture of the daughter of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people lightly, \q saying, "Peace, peace," \q and there is no peace.

R.11: My people are badly hurt, but the leaders treat the wound as if it were only a scratch. \q They say, "Peace, peace!" \q But there is no peace.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: my people, spoken of with tender love
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the whole people as a beloved daughter, as "daughter Zion" pictures the city. It is a word of affection and grief, and Jeremiah uses it more than any other book (4:11; 6:26; 8:19, 21-23; 9:6; 14:17; Lamentations 2:11; 4:3). It means the people themselves, not a part of them.

decisions.choice: the same words as 6:14, with "daughter of" added
decisions.reason: 6:14 says "the fracture of my people"; here it is "the fracture of the daughter of my people". The rest is word for word the same, and it is rendered the same way here. The "peace, peace" of the false prophets is the main note at 6:14.

decisions.choice: peace: safety and well-being, no disaster coming
decisions.reason: As in 6:14. The prophets and priests promise that all will be well, while the nation's injury is fatal.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people (L); my dear people (B); my people (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of a daughter. Balanced keeps the tenderness of the phrase with "dear" but not the picture, and Readable says "my people". The same wording is used wherever the phrase comes in Jeremiah and Lamentations.

decisions.choice: the leaders treat the wound as if it were only a scratch
decisions.reason: As in 6:14, Readable names the prophets and priests of verse 10 as "the leaders" and puts "healed lightly" as a picture of treating a deep wound as a scratch.

records.source: הֹבִ֕שׁוּ כִּ֥י תוֹעֵבָ֖ה עָשׂ֑וּ גַּם־בּ֣וֹשׁ לֹֽא־יֵבֹ֗שׁוּ וְהִכָּלֵם֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ לָכֵ֞ן יִפְּל֣וּ בַנֹּפְלִ֗ים בְּעֵ֧ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֛ם יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Are they ashamed that abomination they have done? Also be ashamed not they are ashamed, and to blush not they know; therefore they will fall among the falling; in [the] time of their visitation they will stumble, says Yahweh.
pieces: Were they ashamed when they did such detestable things? \q Not in the least; they have forgotten how to blush. \q So they will fall with the fallen; \q when the time comes to call them to account they will be brought down, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: Were they ashamed when they did abomination? \q No, they were not at all ashamed, and they did not know how to blush. \q Therefore they will fall among those who fall; \q at the time of their punishment they will stumble, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: They have done disgusting things. Do they feel ashamed? \q No, not at all! They have not even learned how to blush. \q That is why they will die with all the others who die. \q When the time comes to punish them, they will fall, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the same words as 6:15, with "the time of their punishment"
decisions.reason: 6:15 says "at the time I punish them"; here it is "at the time of their punishment". The meaning is the same, and the rest of the verse matches 6:15 word for word.

decisions.choice: their punishment: the time God calls them to account
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "to visit", used of God coming to inspect and to deal with what he finds. Here it is the day he punishes their sin (as 6:15; 10:15).

decisions.choice: the wording of 6:15
decisions.reason: Each level follows 6:15, changing only the last line to fit "the time of their punishment".

records.source: אָסֹ֥ף אֲסִיפֵ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֑ה אֵין֩ עֲנָבִ֨ים בַּגֶּ֜פֶן וְאֵ֧ין תְּאֵנִ֣ים בַּתְּאֵנָ֗ה וְהֶֽעָלֶה֙ נָבֵ֔ל וָאֶתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם יַעַבְרֽוּם׃
records.gloss: Gathering I will make an end of them, declares Yahweh; there are no grapes on the vine, and no figs on the fig tree, and the leaf has withered; and [what] I gave to them will pass from them.
pieces: I will gather them in and put an end to them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q There are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree; even the leaves have withered. \q What I gave them will pass away from them.

L.13: I will surely gather and make an end of them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q there are no grapes on the vine, and no figs on the fig tree, and the leaf has withered; \q and what I gave them will pass away from them.

R.13: I will gather them up and finish them off, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q There are no grapes on the vines and no figs on the fig trees. Even the leaves have dried up. \q So the things I gave them will be taken away.

decisions.choice: I will surely gather and make an end of them: a play on two similar verbs
alternatives: I will surely gather their harvest
decisions.reason: The first word comes from the verb "to gather", used of bringing in a harvest; the second, as the Hebrew is vowelled, comes from a verb meaning "to bring to an end". Together they say that God will gather his people in like a harvest, to finish them (Zephaniah 1:2-3 has the same pair). The letters can also be read "I will gather their harvest", which leads into the empty vine and fig tree.

decisions.choice: no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree: God finds no fruit in his people
decisions.reason: God planted Israel as a choice vine (2:21; Isaiah 5:1-7) and looks for fruit, but finds none (Micah 7:1; Hosea 9:10). The nominal clauses describe what he finds now; the leaf withering shows a tree that is dying.

decisions.choice: what I gave them will pass away from them: a short, hard clause
alternatives: I have given them over to those who will pass over them
decisions.reason: The last words are very brief and their sense is not certain. As read here, the land and its gifts that God gave will be lost to them (Deuteronomy 28:33). The Greek translation (the Septuagint) does not have this clause.

decisions.choice: put an end to them (B); finish them off (R); will be taken away (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the two verbs of the first line in plain words; Readable adds "So" to show the link between the barren vine and what is lost.

records.source: עַל־מָה֙ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ יֹֽשְׁבִ֔ים הֵֽאָסְפ֗וּ וְנָב֛וֹא אֶל־עָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָ֖ר וְנִדְּמָה־שָּׁ֑ם כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֤ינוּ הֲדִמָּ֨נוּ֙ וַיַּשְׁקֵ֣נוּ מֵי־רֹ֔אשׁ כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אנוּ לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: On what [are] we sitting? Gather yourselves, and let us go into the cities of the fortification, and let us perish there; for Yahweh our God has made us perish and has given us to drink water of poison, for we have sinned against Yahweh.
pieces: "Why are we sitting here? \q Come together, let us go into the fortified cities and meet our end there; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has doomed us to die and made us drink poisoned water, \q because we have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: "Why are we sitting still? \q Gather yourselves, and let us go into the fortified cities and perish there; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has made us perish and has given us poisoned water to drink, \q because we have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: The people say, "Why are we just sitting here? \q Let us all go into the cities with strong walls and die there. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God has decided that we must die. He has given us poison to drink, \q because we have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: why are we sitting?: the people of Judah speak, through verse 15
decisions.reason: The voice changes with no word of introduction: "we" are the people of the countryside, hearing of the enemy's approach. They call on one another to flee into the walled towns, as in 4:5, but now with no hope of escape there.

decisions.choice: perish ... made us perish: be silenced, brought to the stillness of death
decisions.reason: The verb means to be still or silent, and also to be destroyed, brought to the silence of death (47:5; 48:2). Both senses may be heard: they will sit silent in the cities, and there they will die, because God has given them over to it.

decisions.choice: poisoned water: a bitter, poisonous drink
decisions.reason: The word is the name of a bitter, poisonous plant (Deuteronomy 29:17; Hosea 10:4). God giving his people such water to drink is a picture of judgment they must swallow (9:14; 23:15).

decisions.choice: The people say
decisions.reason: Readable names the speakers, which the Hebrew leaves the reader to work out (meaning decision m1).

records.source: קַוֵּ֥ה לְשָׁל֖וֹם וְאֵ֣ין ט֑וֹב לְעֵ֥ת מַרְפֵּ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה בְעָתָֽה׃
records.gloss: Hoping for peace, and there is no good; for a time of healing, and look, terror.
pieces: We hoped for peace, but nothing good came; \q for a time of healing, but there was only terror."

L.15: Hoping for peace, but no good [came]; \q for a time of healing, and look, terror."

R.15: We hoped for peace, but nothing good happened. \q We hoped for a time of healing, but now there is only terror."

decisions.choice: hoping: the people still speaking, "we hoped"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the verb's bare form, with no person. It carries on the people's words from verse 14: they waited for peace, as their prophets had promised (verse 11), and terror came instead.

decisions.choice: the same words return at 14:19
decisions.reason: The people say almost exactly the same thing in 14:19. The "healing" they hoped for answers the false healing of verse 11.

decisions.choice: We hoped
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "we", the people who speak in verse 14.

records.source: מִדָּ֤ן נִשְׁמַע֙ נַחְרַ֣ת סוּסָ֗יו מִקּוֹל֙ מִצְהֲל֣וֹת אַבִּירָ֔יו רָעֲשָׁ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּב֗וֹאוּ וַיֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ וּמְלוֹאָ֔הּ עִ֖יר וְיֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: From Dan is heard [the] snorting of his horses; at [the] sound of [the] neighings of his mighty ones quakes all the land; and they have come and devoured [the] land and its fullness, [the] city and those dwelling in it.
pieces: The snorting of the enemy's horses is heard from Dan; at the neighing of his stallions \q the whole land shakes. \q They come and devour the land and all that is in it, \q the city with its people.

L.16: From Dan is heard the snorting of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his stallions \q the whole land quakes; \q they have come and devoured the land and all that fills it, \q the city and those who live in it.

R.16: The snorting of the enemy's horses can be heard from the town of Dan in the north. When his strong horses neigh, \q the whole land shakes with fear. \q The enemy comes and destroys the land and everything in it, \q the city and all the people who live there.

decisions.choice: from Dan: from the far north of the land
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel ("from Dan to Beersheba", 1 Samuel 3:20). The invader comes from the north (1:14; 4:15-16), and the news of his coming is heard there first.

decisions.choice: his mighty ones: his stallions
decisions.reason: The word means mighty or strong ones. Next to "horses" it means the war horses, as in 47:3 and 50:11.

decisions.choice: quakes ... they have come and devoured: the coming disaster seen as already here
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for completed action. The prophet sees the invasion so clearly that he tells it as done.

decisions.choice: the enemy's horses; the town of Dan in the north (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his horses" without naming the rider; Balanced and Readable say "the enemy". Readable says where Dan was.

records.source: כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י מְשַׁלֵּ֜חַ בָּכֶ֗ם נְחָשִׁים֙ צִפְעֹנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־לָהֶ֖ם לָ֑חַשׁ וְנִשְּׁכ֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: For look, I [am] sending among you snakes, vipers, which there is not for them charming, and they will bite you, declares Yahweh.
pieces: For I am about to send snakes among you, \q vipers that no charmer can control, \q and they will bite you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.17: For look, I am sending among you snakes, \q vipers that cannot be charmed, \q and they will bite you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.17: I am going to send poisonous snakes among you. \q No one can use magic to stop them. \q They will bite you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: cannot be charmed: no snake charmer can stop them
decisions.reason: Snake charmers who tamed snakes with spells or music were well known (Psalm 58:5-6; Ecclesiastes 10:11). These snakes are beyond every charm: no skill or ritual will turn the judgment aside.

decisions.choice: vipers: a deadly kind of snake, exact kind unknown
decisions.reason: The word names a poisonous snake (Isaiah 11:8; 59:5). Here the snakes stand for the invading army, as in the plague of snakes in the wilderness (Numbers 21:6).

decisions.choice: No one can use magic to stop them
decisions.reason: Readable explains snake charming in plain words.

records.source: מַבְלִ֥יגִיתִ֖י עֲלֵ֣י יָג֑וֹן עָלַ֖י לִבִּ֥י דַוָּֽי׃
records.gloss: My cheer [is gone]; upon me [is] sorrow; upon me my heart [is] faint.
pieces: My joy is gone; grief has come over me; \q my heart is sick within me.

L.18: My cheer [is gone]; sorrow [is] upon me; \q my heart is faint within me.

R.18: I have no joy left, only sorrow. \q My heart is sick inside me.

decisions.choice: my cheer is gone; sorrow is upon me: the first word is uncertain
decisions.reason: The first word appears nowhere else. As the Hebrew is vowelled it seems to mean "my cheer" or "my source of comfort", so the line says that the speaker's joy has given way to sorrow. If the letters are divided differently they read "without healing", giving "my sorrow is beyond healing". Either way the speaker is overcome by grief.

decisions.choice: the speaker: Jeremiah, grieving over his people
decisions.reason: From here to verse 23 the voice is that of one who mourns for "the daughter of my people". It is most naturally the prophet himself, who shares the pain of the judgment he announces; but God speaks in the middle of verse 19, and some hear God's own grief in these lines. The voices are left as they come.

decisions.choice: [is gone] (L); is gone (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb. Literal brackets the words supplied; Balanced supplies them plainly.

records.heading: Is there no balm in Gilead?

records.source: הִנֵּה־ק֞וֹל שַֽׁוְעַ֣ת בַּת־עַמִּ֗י מֵאֶ֨רֶץ֙ מַרְחַקִּ֔ים הַֽיהוָה֙ אֵ֣ין בְּצִיּ֔וֹן אִם־מַלְכָּ֖הּ אֵ֣ין בָּ֑הּ מַדּ֗וּעַ הִכְעִס֛וּנִי בִּפְסִלֵיהֶ֖ם בְּהַבְלֵ֥י נֵכָֽר׃
records.gloss: Look, [the] sound of [the] cry for help of [the] daughter of my people from a land of distances: [Is] Yahweh not in Zion? Or her king, not [is he] in her? Why have they provoked me with their images, with vanities of foreignness?
pieces: Listen! The cry of my dear people for help comes from a land far away: \q "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} not in Zion? \q Is her King no longer there?" \q Why have they made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with their idols, with worthless foreign gods?

L.19: Listen, the sound of the cry of the daughter of my people from a land far away: \q "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} not in Zion? \q Is her King not in her?" \q Why have they provoked {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with their carved images, with foreign worthless things?

R.19: Listen! My people are crying for help from a land far away. \q They ask, "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} not in Zion anymore? \q Is Zion's King not there?" \q Why have they made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry by worshiping their idols and useless foreign gods?

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

decisions.choice: from a land far away: from exile, or from every part of the wide land
alternatives: from the length and breadth of the land
decisions.reason: The words mean "from a land of great distances". They may picture the people already carried into exile and crying out from far away, or the cry rising from one end of the land to the other (Isaiah 33:17 uses the phrase of a land stretching far).

decisions.choice: why have they provoked me?: God answers the people's question
decisions.reason: The people ask whether the LORD, Zion's King, has left his city, since he does not save them. God breaks in with his own question: they are the ones who left him for idols. Then the people's lament goes on in verse 20.

decisions.choice: carved images ... foreign worthless things: idols of other nations
decisions.reason: The first word is an image carved from wood or stone. The second means "breath" or "vapor", Jeremiah's word for idols that are empty and worthless (2:5; 10:8, 15); they are "foreign" because they are the gods of other peoples.

decisions.choice: They ask; Zion's King; by worshiping
decisions.reason: Readable introduces the people's question, says whose King is meant, and states how the idols provoked God.

records.source: עָבַ֥ר קָצִ֖יר כָּ֣לָה קָ֑יִץ וַאֲנַ֖חְנוּ ל֥וֹא נוֹשָֽׁעְנוּ׃
records.gloss: Has passed harvest, has ended summer, and we not have been saved.
pieces: "The harvest is over and the summer is gone, \q and still we are not saved."

L.20: "Harvest has passed, summer has come to an end, \q and we have not been saved."

R.20: "Harvest time has come and gone, and summer is over. \q But still no one has saved us."

decisions.choice: harvest ... summer: the grain harvest and then the summer fruit
decisions.reason: The grain was harvested in spring and early summer, and the grapes, figs and other summer fruit gathered at the end of summer. When both seasons have passed and nothing has been gathered, there is no hope of food until next year. It may be a saying of the people: season after season has gone by, and the help they waited for has not come.

decisions.choice: we are not saved: the people speaking again
decisions.reason: The "we" is the people, as in verses 14-15, and their words are set as speech. They could also be the prophet's own summary of the people's plight.

decisions.choice: saved: rescued from the enemy
decisions.reason: The verb means to be rescued or delivered, here from the invader and the famine. Rescue was what they expected from the LORD in Zion (verse 19).

decisions.choice: no one has saved us
decisions.reason: Readable turns the passive into an active sentence.

records.source: עַל־שֶׁ֥בֶר בַּת־עַמִּ֖י הָשְׁבָּ֑רְתִּי קָדַ֕רְתִּי שַׁמָּ֖ה הֶחֱזִקָֽתְנִי׃
records.gloss: Over [the] brokenness of [the] daughter of my people I am broken; I go in mourning; horror has seized me.
pieces: Because my dear people are broken, I am broken; \q I mourn, and horror has taken hold of me.

L.21: For the brokenness of the daughter of my people I am broken; \q I go about in mourning; horror has seized me.

R.21: My people are crushed, so I am crushed too. \q I am full of sorrow, and horror has taken hold of me.

decisions.choice: the brokenness ... I am broken: the same word for the people and for the one who mourns
decisions.reason: The noun is the "fracture" of verse 11. The mourner shares the people's wound: as they are broken, so is he.

decisions.choice: I go about in mourning: dark, like one who mourns
decisions.reason: The verb means to be dark, and then to go about in mourning, dressed in dark clothes and unwashed (14:2; Psalm 38:7).

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

decisions.choice: crushed ... crushed too
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the repeated word with "crushed", which says plainly what the picture of a broken bone means.

records.source: הַצֳרִי֙ אֵ֣ין בְּגִלְעָ֔ד אִם־רֹפֵ֖א אֵ֣ין שָׁ֑ם כִּ֗י מַדּ֨וּעַ֙ לֹ֣א עָֽלְתָ֔ה אֲרֻכַ֖ת בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: [Is] balm not in Gilead? Or [is] a physician not there? For why has not come up [the] healing of [the] daughter of my people?
pieces: Is there no balm in Gilead? \q Is there no doctor there? \q Why then has the wound of my dear people \q not been healed?

L.22: Is there no balm in Gilead? \q Is there no physician there? \q Why then has the healing of the daughter of my people \q not come up?

R.22: Is there no healing balm in Gilead? \q Is there no doctor there? \q Then why have my people \q not been healed?

decisions.choice: balm in Gilead: a famous healing resin from east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead, the hill country east of the Jordan, was known for a fragrant resin used to treat wounds; traders carried it to Egypt (Genesis 37:25; 43:11). Jeremiah mentions it again for Egypt and Babylon, whose wounds it cannot heal (46:11; 51:8). The cure is near at hand, yet the people are not healed.

decisions.choice: the healing has not come up: new flesh has not grown over the wound
decisions.reason: The noun means the new skin that grows over a wound as it heals, and "come up" pictures it rising on the wound (30:17; 33:6). The wound of verse 11 stays open.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

decisions.choice: doctor; the wound ... not been healed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "doctor" for the physician and say plainly that the wound has not healed, which is what the picture of new skin coming up means.

records.source: מִֽי־יִתֵּ֤ן רֹאשִׁי֙ מַ֔יִם וְעֵינִ֖י מְק֣וֹר דִּמְעָ֑ה וְאֶבְכֶּה֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה אֵ֖ת חַֽלְלֵ֥י בַת־עַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Who will give [that] my head [were] waters and my eyes a fountain of tears, and I would weep day and night [for the] slain of [the] daughter of my people!
pieces: If only my head were all water \q and my eyes a fountain of tears, \q so that I could weep day and night \q for the slain of my dear people!

L.23: Who will make my head waters \q and my eyes a fountain of tears, \q so that I may weep day and night \q for the slain of the daughter of my people!

R.23: I wish my head were full of water \q and my eyes were a fountain of tears! \q Then I could cry day and night \q for my people who have been killed.

decisions.choice: This verse is 8:23 in the Hebrew text, 9:1 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text ends chapter 8 with this verse and begins chapter 9 with "Who will give me in the wilderness a travelers' lodging". Many Bibles number this verse 9:1, so their 9:2-26 is 9:1-25 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates. The verse closes the lament of 8:18-22.

decisions.choice: who will give ...: a wish, "if only"
decisions.reason: "Who will give?" is the Hebrew way of saying "if only" or "I wish" (Deuteronomy 5:26; Psalm 14:7).

decisions.choice: my head waters, my eyes a fountain of tears: grief greater than tears can hold
decisions.reason: The mourner wishes for a head full of water and eyes that flow like a spring, so that his weeping would never run dry. Jeremiah's tears for his people return in 9:17; 13:17; 14:17 and Lamentations 1:16; 2:11, 18.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.
